cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a black-and-white cotton tunic with colourful embroidered diamonds, stripes, and circular motifs, matching the museum's description of a garment worn by the claimed group; this style of embroidered tunic is consistent with Central African garment traditions such as the Gbaya.

physical.title: tunic
physical.summary: Tunic; made of cotton; bodice piece of black cotton folded in half, trimmed along sides with white cotton; round hole cut at top for head; decorated with red and green stripe of embroidery around neck opening, red, green and blue groups of diamonds, red and green star with yellow centre, white, yellow, red and green circles down centre; skirt made of vertical strips of white and black cotton sewn together, decorated with red, green, yellow and blue embroidered diamonds; two oval holes circled with red embroidery cut on front of skirt, piece of multicoloured cotton sewn behind to make pocket; strip of multicoloured cotton sewn in at bottom corner on each side attaching front to back of skirt.
